payload.summary: Reviewed the cited shrimp, substrate, and preset code paths. All six amendments describe real technical issues: four runtime correctness bugs in molt handling/config plumbing, one layered-substrate diffusion correctness bug, and one maintainability defect from an undocumented hardcoded process rate.

votes.rationale: In `molt_cycle`, mixed-outcome days set `last_molt_success` to `false` when any stage fails, but the accumulator still applies the success decrement, so `failed_molt_accum` can improve on the same tick. That leaves two downstream signals disagreeing about whether the molt cycle went well, and `subadult_to_adult` reads the boolean gate directly. This is a real state-consistency bug with behavioral impact.

`step_substrate_zones` computes a single O2 boundary for the full stacked bed, but `effective_substrate_porosity` uses only the first non-zero layer's porosity. Once the predicted boundary extends below that layer, deeper-layer porosity has no influence on diffusion at all, which is not consistent with a layered-bed model. That is a correctness defect in the current penetration calculation, not merely a cosmetic refinement.

The `0.01` detritus-consumption factor is an undocumented scientific parameter embedded directly in the respiration path, while the analogous periphyton term is exposed through `process_params`. That makes calibration asymmetric and hides an important model assumption from config and provenance tooling. Even if the numeric value stays the same, leaving it as a magic constant is a maintainability and robustness defect.

Fresh stocked states satisfy the migration guard because `inter_molt_timer_days` defaults to `14.0` and all per-stage timers default to `0.0`. The migration branch therefore seeds every stage timer from the legacy field on the first daily tick, so new cohorts do not start from a clean per-stage cadence. Existing tests already work around this by zeroing `inter_molt_timer_days`, which reinforces that this is a real initialization bug.

The accumulator logic collapses all same-day stage outcomes into `any_failed` and `any_succeeded` booleans. That means two or three failed stages still contribute only one `+0.3`, and a mixed failure/success day can net a decrease because both branches run. This undercounts failure pressure exactly on overlap days and is a distinct defect from the boolean/accumulator disagreement in `last_molt_success`.

The TOML preset defines five shrimp knobs that are absent from `ShrimpPreset`, absent from the metadata lookup helpers, and never copied into `ShrimpRuntimeParams`. Because unknown keys are ignored during deserialization here, the file still loads while silently discarding those settings. That is a real configuration bug and a maintenance trap, even though the current literal values happen to match runtime defaults.
